Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

119:`plan_chain_prune(paths, checkpoint, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` builds a read-only signed plan for trimming persisted convergence archives, reading the archive files but never modifying, creating or deleting them. `paths` is an explicit, non-empty list of distinct file paths; each archive is one version-1 canonical JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing `\n`) carrying exactly `project` (a unique non-empty identifier), `certificate` and the ordered `rounds` (each `{confirmation, seq}`, numbered consecutively from one), with the certificate and every confirmation carried as non-empty lowercase hex bytes. The sealing `checkpoint` is a `seal_chain_checkpoint` packet authenticated against the current keyring through the exact `verify_chain_suffix` rules (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`, no fallback). An archive is eligible for pruning only when its certificate digest is part of the checkpoint's pruned evidence prefix and its whole round group re-verifies through the exact `verify_fork_convergence` rules against `decision`, `policy` and `keyring` at `moment`; non-eligible archives are retained and when nothing is eligible a `ValueError` is raised. The result is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object with no trailing byte; the payload binds exactly `checkpoint` (its SHA-256), `delete` (eligible projects ascending), `retain` (the SHA-256 of every retained archive's bytes, ascending), `source` and `target` (each a map from an eligible project to the digest of its archive bytes before pruning and of its trimmed project-marker archive afterwards) and `version` (integer 1). It carries no moment or project identifier of its own and is signed with the checkpoint's own exact issuer/key, so equal arguments produce byte-identical plans. Container/field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty/duplicate path or project, a wrong key set or an illegal version raises `ValueError`; a missing archive raises `FileNotFoundError`; an illegal archive or checkpoint raises `InvalidPruneError`; credential and signature faults raise `AuthenticationError`.
121:`prune_chain_archives(items, keyring)` executes the plans in one controlled batch. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id`, an archive `path`, the signed `plan`, the sealing `checkpoint` and a `header` naming the exact signing `issuer`/`keyVersion` (the checkpoint sealer) and the non-negative prune `moment`; the batch structure and keyring are validated first. Each item then runs in strict input order and full isolation: bad credentials, malformed plans or checkpoints and stale archives are recorded for that item alone, the archive is left unchanged and the batch continues. When the archive at `path` hashes to the plan's source digest for its project, the planned trimmed target (one canonical `{project, version}` marker ending in one `\n`, the certificate and all round bytes gone) is installed in a crash-safe two-phase transaction, and the receipt status is `pruned`; when the archive already hashes to the target digest nothing is written and the status is `duplicate`; any other content records `StalePruneError`. An `OSError` raised while writing, flushing, syncing a file or directory, replacing or deleting is recorded for that item with its original text and leaves the retryable transaction material in place. The transaction uses only same-directory files — a unique candidate, the hard-linked predecessor and the `path + ".prune.txn"` intent — whose only phases are `prepared` and `installed`; unrelated files are never scanned or touched. The batch returns, in input order, fresh dicts keyed `id`, `receipt` and `error`. The receipt is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object binding the `status`, the complete plan, the `checkpoint` digest, `beforeDigest`/`afterDigest` (equal for a duplicate), the full `delete` and `retain` digests, the prune `moment` and `version` 1, signed under the exact header key. The first completion and a same-plan re-entry (an interrupted transaction whose `.prune.txn` intent is still present) return one identical signed receipt: an installed same-plan intent is completed to the original `pruned` receipt and a prepared one is rolled back and retried.
123:`recover_chain_prune(path)` settles one interrupted prune transaction, touching only the files its `path + ".prune.txn"` intent names. With no intent it returns `clean` without scanning artifacts, with the current archive digest (or `None` when the path is missing). A `prepared` intent rolls the source bytes back byte-for-byte from the retained predecessor (the path is removed again when it did not exist) and deletes the candidate, reporting `rolled-back`; an `installed` intent requires the current bytes to hash to `newDigest`, removes the remaining artifacts and reports `completed`; the intent is deleted last and the directory synced so a repeat returns `clean`, and every result carries the resulting digest. A non-str path raises `TypeError`; a malformed intent (wrong key set, version, phase, target, name confinement or digest binding, or a missing necessary artifact) raises `InvalidPruneError` without touching unrelated files; an `OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing propagates unchanged with the intent and artifacts retained for a retry. `InvalidPruneError` and `StalePruneError` both subclass `ValueError`. Planning and recovery read files but planning changes nothing; the existing checkpoint continuation verification, replacement chains, module commands and README command surface are unchanged.
125:`verify_prune_receipt(receipt, checkpoint, keyring, moment)` verifies one signed prune receipt entirely offline — only the receipt bytes, the sealing checkpoint bytes, the current keyring and a non-negative moment are consulted, no file is read and no input is modified. The receipt must be a version-1 canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds `afterDigest`, `beforeDigest`, `checkpoint`, `delete`, `moment`, the complete embedded `plan`, `retain`, `status` (`pruned` or `duplicate`) and `version`. The embedded plan must itself be the same canonical version-1 envelope, match the supplied checkpoint digest and signing identity/key version, and the receipt must repeat the plan's delete projects and retain digests exactly — a missing, extra, reordered or replaced entry is a broken binding. The checkpoint, plan and receipt signatures are all recomputed with the single key the checkpoint currently names (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`) with no fallback. The unique plan target project is located solely from the status and before/after digests (zero or several candidates reject); the verifier then regenerates that project's version-1 prune marker itself, hashes its complete bytes, and requires the recomputed digest to match both the plan target and the receipt `afterDigest` — the receipt's derived conclusion is never trusted; a `pruned` receipt's `beforeDigest` must match the source archive and a `duplicate` receipt's both digests must match the target marker. It returns a fresh dict with the fixed key order `project`, `status`, `beforeDigest`, `afterDigest`, `checkpoint`, `planDigest`, `moment` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal, independent new objects. A wrong public argument type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int) and an illegal moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal encoding, key set, version, digest, status or binding raises `InvalidPruneReceiptError` (a `ValueError` subclass, distinct from `InvalidPruneError`); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or any signature error raise `AuthenticationError`.
127:`verify_prune_receipts(items, keyring, moment)` verifies a batch of prune receipts offline. Each item holds exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes; the non-empty list, keyring and moment are pre-validated in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/field faults `TypeError`, a bool rejected as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal moment `ValueError`). Each item is then verified in strict input order and in isolation through the exact `verify_prune_receipt` rules, reported as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated`; one item's failure never stops later items. The top-level result has exactly the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1), and each report carries in fixed order `error` (`None` when verified, otherwise a definite non-empty message), `id`, `result` (a fresh single-entry result when verified, otherwise `None`) and `status`; repeated calls return equal but independent results.
128:## Signed prune attestations and multi-site threshold adjudication
130:`sign_prune_attestation(items, batch, keyring, moment, site, version)` hands the conclusion of a prune receipt batch verification to an offline adjudicator. It takes the same non-empty `items` list as `verify_prune_receipts` (each item exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the signed `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes), the authorized non-empty `batch` id, a `keyring`, the signing `moment` and the exact signing `site` and key `version`. The batch runs through the existing `verify_prune_receipts` verification in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/public-field type faults `TypeError`, a bool never posing as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong item key set, an empty batch or site or a non-positive/non-int version `ValueError`); one receipt's own failure is never raised. The `invalid` and `unauthenticated` items are kept exactly as the batch reported them — status, definite error text, a null `result` and all — and no trusted identity, project or boundary is ever filled in for them. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`. The payload binds exactly `batch`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `site` and `version` (integer 1); each item, in the original input order with no sorting, deduplication or replacement, carries exactly `checkpoint` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that item's checkpoint bytes), `id`, `receipt` (the SHA-256 of that item's receipt bytes) and `report` (that item's complete batch verification report, bound verbatim, with a verified report's result naming the same checkpoint digest). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key the keyring binds to the exact site and version with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.
132:`adjudicate_prune_attestations(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates uniquely identified site attestations into one signed threshold decision, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `attestation` bytes. The `policy` carries exactly `batch` (the authorized batch id), `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the number of sites); `keyring` and `moment` keep their existing rules and `issuer`/`version` name the adjudicator credentials. Every attestation is re-checked by the exact signing site and key version named in its payload with no fallback: a structurally illegal packet is recorded `invalid-proof`, unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature `unauthenticated`, and a wrong batch, an unauthorized site or an unauthorized key version `unauthorized` — each rejecting only that item while the others continue. For one site, a packet counts only when the complete report and every receipt/checkpoint byte digest all agree; an exact repeat of the same content is `duplicate` and different valid content from one site is a `contradiction`. 19408	def _tally_prune_rows(
19409	    rows: list[dict], threshold: int
19410	) -> tuple[str, dict | None]:
19411	    """Mark duplicate/contradiction rows and derive the overall status.
19412	
19413	    Rows from one site are the same attestation only when their complete
19414	    authenticated entries agree byte for byte (every receipt/checkpoint
19415	    digest and every report); the smallest-id packet of one identical
19416	    group is the vote and exact repeats are duplicates, while distinct
19417	    contents from one site contradict each other.  Distinct sites must
19418	    agree on that same complete content -- any report or bound digest
19419	    disagreement conflicts and no majority can outvote it.
19420	
19421	    A conflict of either kind binds no report.  Otherwise the one
19422	    unique agreed content, when one exists, always carries its common
19423	    report: backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites the
19424	    tally is ``accepted``, and short of the threshold it stays
19425	    ``insufficient`` but keeps that unique report.  With no valid vote
19426	    at all the tally is ``insufficient`` with the report null.
19427	    """
19428	    by_site: dict[str, dict[bytes, list[dict]]] = {}
19429	    for row in rows:
19430	        if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] in (
19431	            PA_CONCLUSION_VALID,
19432	            PA_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE,
19433	            PA_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION,
19434	        ):
19435	            content = _prune_compact(row[PA_ENTRIES])
19436	            by_site.setdefault(row[ADJ_SITE], {}).setdefault(
19437	                content, []
19438	            ).append(row)
19439	
19440	    contradicted = False
19441	    votes: dict[str, bytes] = {}
19442	    representatives: dict[str, dict] = {}
19443	    for site, groups in by_site.items():
19444	        if len(groups) > 1:
19445	            contradicted = True
19446	            ordered_groups = sorted(
19447	                groups.values(),
19448	                key=lambda members: min(member[ID] for member in members),
19449	            )
19450	            for members in ordered_groups:
19451	                members.sort(key=lambda row: row[ID])
19452	                members[0][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = PA_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION
19453	                members[0][ADJ_REASON] = REASON_CONTRADICTION
19454	                for extra in members[1:]:
19455	                    extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = PA_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
19456	                    extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
19457	        else:
19458	            content, members = next(iter(groups.items()))
19459	            members.sort(key=lambda row: row[ID])
19460	            members[0][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = PA_CONCLUSION_VALID
19461	            members[0][ADJ_REASON] = None
19462	            for extra in members[1:]:
19463	                extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = PA_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
19464	                extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
19465	            votes[site] = content
19466	            representatives[site] = members[0]
19467	
19468	    contents = set(votes.values())
19469	    if contradicted or len(contents) > 1:
19470	        return PA_STATUS_CONFLICTED, None
19471	    if len(contents) == 1:
19472	        first_site = min(votes)
19473	        common_report = _common_prune_report(
19474	            representatives[first_site][PA_ENTRIES]
19475	        )
19476	        if len(votes) >= threshold:
19477	            return PA_STATUS_ACCEPTED, common_report
19478	        # Unique, conflict-free evidence short of the threshold keeps
19479	        # the one common report but cannot be accepted yet.
19480	        return PA_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT, common_report
19481	    return PA_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT, None

# Offline Autonomous Node Coordination

Minimal backend baseline for autonomous nodes that must keep working during long network outages and later reconcile state with explainable rules.

Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.

```bash
python -m offline_coordination status
python -m offline_coordination recovery check LEDGER [LEDGER ...]
python -m offline_coordination recovery run LEDGER [LEDGER ...] --keyring KEYRING --ticket TICKET --moment MOMENT --audit AUDIT
python -m offline_coordination recovery audit AUDIT [--after N] [--limit N]
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The baseline exposes a local status command plus offline ledger recovery operations. Persistent state is available via `offline_coordination.storage` and an append-only hash-chained audit log via `offline_coordination.audit`. Replication, conflict policies, security boundaries, observability, and network services are intentionally left for subsequent tasks.

The root is verified under the first policy's sites and threshold; every successor re-recomputes its verdict from the bound full evidence under its new policy at the hop's effective moment, re-checks the root, predecessor and height links, the old/new policy digests and version step, the non-decreasing effective moment and the append-only evidence prefix, re-applies the verdict state machine and dual-policy sealer authorization, requires the settled verdict to still hold with credentials usable at `moment`, and verifies the HMAC. It returns a fresh mapping with exactly `rootDigest`, `headDigest`, `height` (0 for a bare root), `policyVersion` and `status`; a bad root raises `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError`, a bad successor `InvalidChainError` and a signature or credential fault `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_decision_chains(items, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a whole batch offline. Each item holds exactly a unique `id`, its `roots` packet, its ordered `successors` packets and its per-stage `policies`; the batch and shared materials are pre-validated in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/field faults `TypeError`; an empty list, empty or duplicate id or wrong key set `ValueError`). Each chain is then reported in strict input order, in isolation, as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated` with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`. One predecessor digest pointing at two distinct successor digests is a fork; a mere prefix extension (one chain growing longer along the same packets) is not. Every verified chain crossing a forking edge is reclassified `conflicted` with its verified result retained; chains that were invalid or unauthenticated are never reclassified. The result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1).

`seal_decision_head(items, target, decision, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` seals a stable anchor only for the `target` chain within the batch that is `verified` (not conflicted by a fork), whose head is `accepted`. The anchor binds the target's root digest, head digest and height together with the head policy digest, head policy version and sealing moment and is signed under the exact issuer/version key; sealing a batch that is not entirely pre-validated, an unknown or empty target, a non-accepted/forked target or an illegal version raises `ValueError`, and a credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`. `verify_decision_head(anchor, items, target, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks the anchor structurally and its HMAC against the current key, re-runs the original batch and confirms the target still verifies, is accepted and unforked, and that every bound digest, height and version still matches; it returns `rootDigest`, `headDigest`, `height`, `policyDigest`, `policyVersion` and `anchorDigest`. A bad anchor raises `InvalidAnchorError` (a `ValueError` subclass); a batch fault raises the underlying `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError` or `InvalidChainError`; a signature or credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`. The adjudication, certificate, recovery command and `status` interfaces are unchanged and no new command-line entry is added.

## Pruning multi-round convergence archives

`plan_chain_prune(paths, checkpoint, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` builds a read-only signed plan for trimming persisted convergence archives, reading the archive files but never modifying, creating or deleting them. `paths` is an explicit, non-empty list of distinct file paths; each archive is one version-1 canonical JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing `\n`) carrying exactly `project` (a unique non-empty identifier), `certificate` and the ordered `rounds` (each `{confirmation, seq}`, numbered consecutively from one), with the certificate and every confirmation carried as non-empty lowercase hex bytes. The sealing `checkpoint` is a `seal_chain_checkpoint` packet authenticated against the current keyring through the exact `verify_chain_suffix` rules (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`, no fallback). An archive is eligible for pruning only when its certificate digest is part of the checkpoint's pruned evidence prefix and its whole round group re-verifies through the exact `verify_fork_convergence` rules against `decision`, `policy` and `keyring` at `moment`; non-eligible archives are retained and when nothing is eligible a `ValueError` is raised. The result is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object with no trailing byte; the payload binds exactly `checkpoint` (its SHA-256), `delete` (eligible projects ascending), `retain` (the SHA-256 of every retained archive's bytes, ascending), `source` and `target` (each a map from an eligible project to the digest of its archive bytes before pruning and of its trimmed project-marker archive afterwards) and `version` (integer 1). It carries no moment or project identifier of its own and is signed with the checkpoint's own exact issuer/key, so equal arguments produce byte-identical plans. Container/field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty/duplicate path or project, a wrong key set or an illegal version raises `ValueError`; a missing archive raises `FileNotFoundError`; an illegal archive or checkpoint raises `InvalidPruneError`; credential and signature faults raise `AuthenticationError`.

`prune_chain_archives(items, keyring)` executes the plans in one controlled batch. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id`, an archive `path`, the signed `plan`, the sealing `checkpoint` and a `header` naming the exact signing `issuer`/`keyVersion` (the checkpoint sealer) and the non-negative prune `moment`; the batch structure and keyring are validated first. Each item then runs in strict input order and full isolation: bad credentials, malformed plans or checkpoints and stale archives are recorded for that item alone, the archive is left unchanged and the batch continues. When the archive at `path` hashes to the plan's source digest for its project, the planned trimmed target (one canonical `{project, version}` marker ending in one `\n`, the certificate and all round bytes gone) is installed in a crash-safe two-phase transaction, and the receipt status is `pruned`; when the archive already hashes to the target digest nothing is written and the status is `duplicate`; any other content records `StalePruneError`. An `OSError` raised while writing, flushing, syncing a file or directory, replacing or deleting is recorded for that item with its original text and leaves the retryable transaction material in place. The transaction uses only same-directory files — a unique candidate, the hard-linked predecessor and the `path + ".prune.txn"` intent — whose only phases are `prepared` and `installed`; unrelated files are never scanned or touched. The batch returns, in input order, fresh dicts keyed `id`, `receipt` and `error`. The receipt is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object binding the `status`, the complete plan, the `checkpoint` digest, `beforeDigest`/`afterDigest` (equal for a duplicate), the full `delete` and `retain` digests, the prune `moment` and `version` 1, signed under the exact header key. The first completion and a same-plan re-entry (an interrupted transaction whose `.prune.txn` intent is still present) return one identical signed receipt: an installed same-plan intent is completed to the original `pruned` receipt and a prepared one is rolled back and retried.

`recover_chain_prune(path)` settles one interrupted prune transaction, touching only the files its `path + ".prune.txn"` intent names. With no intent it returns `clean` without scanning artifacts, with the current archive digest (or `None` when the path is missing). A `prepared` intent rolls the source bytes back byte-for-byte from the retained predecessor (the path is removed again when it did not exist) and deletes the candidate, reporting `rolled-back`; an `installed` intent requires the current bytes to hash to `newDigest`, removes the remaining artifacts and reports `completed`; the intent is deleted last and the directory synced so a repeat returns `clean`, and every result carries the resulting digest. A non-str path raises `TypeError`; a malformed intent (wrong key set, version, phase, target, name confinement or digest binding, or a missing necessary artifact) raises `InvalidPruneError` without touching unrelated files; an `OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing propagates unchanged with the intent and artifacts retained for a retry. `InvalidPruneError` and `StalePruneError` both subclass `ValueError`. Planning and recovery read files but planning changes nothing; the existing checkpoint continuation verification, replacement chains, module commands and README command surface are unchanged.

`verify_prune_receipt(receipt, checkpoint, keyring, moment)` verifies one signed prune receipt entirely offline — only the receipt bytes, the sealing checkpoint bytes, the current keyring and a non-negative moment are consulted, no file is read and no input is modified. The receipt must be a version-1 canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds `afterDigest`, `beforeDigest`, `checkpoint`, `delete`, `moment`, the complete embedded `plan`, `retain`, `status` (`pruned` or `duplicate`) and `version`. The embedded plan must itself be the same canonical version-1 envelope, match the supplied checkpoint digest and signing identity/key version, and the receipt must repeat the plan's delete projects and retain digests exactly — a missing, extra, reordered or replaced entry is a broken binding. The checkpoint, plan and receipt signatures are all recomputed with the single key the checkpoint currently names (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`) with no fallback. The unique plan target project is located solely from the status and before/after digests (zero or several candidates reject); the verifier then regenerates that project's version-1 prune marker itself, hashes its complete bytes, and requires the recomputed digest to match both the plan target and the receipt `afterDigest` — the receipt's derived conclusion is never trusted; a `pruned` receipt's `beforeDigest` must match the source archive and a `duplicate` receipt's both digests must match the target marker. It returns a fresh dict with the fixed key order `project`, `status`, `beforeDigest`, `afterDigest`, `checkpoint`, `planDigest`, `moment` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal, independent new objects. A wrong public argument type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int) and an illegal moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal encoding, key set, version, digest, status or binding raises `InvalidPruneReceiptError` (a `ValueError` subclass, distinct from `InvalidPruneError`); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or any signature error raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_prune_receipts(items, keyring, moment)` verifies a batch of prune receipts offline. Each item holds exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes; the non-empty list, keyring and moment are pre-validated in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/field faults `TypeError`, a bool rejected as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal moment `ValueError`). Each item is then verified in strict input order and in isolation through the exact `verify_prune_receipt` rules, reported as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated`; one item's failure never stops later items. The top-level result has exactly the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1), and each report carries in fixed order `error` (`None` when verified, otherwise a definite non-empty message), `id`, `result` (a fresh single-entry result when verified, otherwise `None`) and `status`; repeated calls return equal but independent results.
## Signed prune attestations and multi-site threshold adjudication

`sign_prune_attestation(items, batch, keyring, moment, site, version)` hands the conclusion of a prune receipt batch verification to an offline adjudicator. It takes the same non-empty `items` list as `verify_prune_receipts` (each item exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the signed `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes), the authorized non-empty `batch` id, a `keyring`, the signing `moment` and the exact signing `site` and key `version`. The batch runs through the existing `verify_prune_receipts` verification in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/public-field type faults `TypeError`, a bool never posing as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong item key set, an empty batch or site or a non-positive/non-int version `ValueError`); one receipt's own failure is never raised. The `invalid` and `unauthenticated` items are kept exactly as the batch reported them — status, definite error text, a null `result` and all — and no trusted identity, project or boundary is ever filled in for them. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`. The payload binds exactly `batch`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `site` and `version` (integer 1); each item, in the original input order with no sorting, deduplication or replacement, carries exactly `checkpoint` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that item's checkpoint bytes), `id`, `receipt` (the SHA-256 of that item's receipt bytes) and `report` (that item's complete batch verification report, bound verbatim, with a verified report's result naming the same checkpoint digest). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key the keyring binds to the exact site and version with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`adjudicate_prune_attestations(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates uniquely identified site attestations into one signed threshold decision, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `attestation` bytes. The `policy` carries exactly `batch` (the authorized batch id), `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the number of sites); `keyring` and `moment` keep their existing rules and `issuer`/`version` name the adjudicator credentials. Every attestation is re-checked by the exact signing site and key version named in its payload with no fallback: a structurally illegal packet is recorded `invalid-proof`, unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature `unauthenticated`, and a wrong batch, an unauthorized site or an unauthorized key version `unauthorized` — each rejecting only that item while the others continue. For one site, a packet counts only when the complete report and every receipt/checkpoint byte digest all agree; an exact repeat of the same content is `duplicate` and different valid content from one site is a `contradiction`. Distinct sites must agree on that same complete content: any cross-site report difference or bound-digest difference is a `conflicted` fork that a majority cannot outvote. A unique conflict-free content backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted` and carries the one common complete report; the same one unique content short of the threshold stays `insufficient` but still carries that common report; a contradiction or disagreement is `conflicted`; and an `insufficient` tally with no valid vote at all binds a null report. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `attestations` (each input attestation's SHA-256 in the original input order), `issuer`, `items` (the per-attestation rows sorted stably by site then id, each carrying `conclusion`, the attestation `digest`, the authenticated `entries` or null, `id`, `keyVersion`, `reason` and `site`), `keyVersion`, `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical compact policy — sites ascending, each site's versions an ascending array), `report` (the common complete `{items, version}` batch report, or null), `status` and `version` (integer 1); the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact adjudicator key. Parameter, container or public-field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, or an illegal batch, policy, threshold, moment, site or version raises `ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_prune_adjudication(adjudication, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such a decision entirely offline from just the decision bytes, the expected `policy`, the current `keyring` and the verification moment, reading and writing no file and modifying no argument. It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes the policy digest, and re-tallies the bound per-attestation rows purely from the signed payload: the original-order attestation digest bindings, the site/id row ordering, same-site duplicate and contradiction markings, cross-site report and digest agreement, the threshold outcome and the claimed common report — any structure, digest, ordering or tally mismatch raises `InvalidPruneAdjudicationError`, which subclasses `ValueError`. It then checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the *current* keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects the decision with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. On success it returns a fresh dict equal to the authenticated payload (`attestations`, `issuer`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `policyDigest`, `report`, `status`, `version`); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects sharing no mutable structure. A non-bytes adjudication or a field of the wrong type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int) and an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`.

`verify_prune_adjudications(items, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty batch of those decisions offline and in strict input order, in isolation. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and the `adjudication` bytes; the whole batch structure, policy, keyring and moment are validated before any adjudication is parsed, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/field type faults `TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`, with policy, keyring and moment keeping their single-entry classification). One decision's failure never stops later items or changes an earlier report. Each item is reported in input order as `verified`, `invalid` (a structure or binding fault, including a tampered status or common report) or `unauthenticated` (unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature), with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`; a failure keeps a definite, non-empty copy of the original exception text and a null result, and a verified item's result is a fresh deep copy of the authenticated adjudication payload. The top-level result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results.

`sign_prune_adjudication_batch(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` packages one such batch verification into an offline handover packet. It takes the same non-empty `items` list as `verify_prune_adjudications` and runs that exact batch verification, so batch-level faults keep the same `TypeError`/`ValueError` classification (an empty issuer or a non-positive version additionally raises `ValueError`) while one decision's failure is never raised. The `invalid` and `unauthenticated` items are kept exactly as reported — status, definite error text and a null result — and no trusted issuer, project or prune boundary is filled in from unauthenticated content. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical compact policy), `items` and `version` (integer 1). Each item, in the original input order with no sorting, deduplication or replacement, carries exactly `id`, `digest` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that item's original adjudication bytes) and `report` (that item's complete batch verification report, including the full authenticated adjudication payload when verified, bound verbatim). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact issuer/version key; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_prune_adjudication_batch(packet, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks a handover packet entirely offline from just the packet bytes, the expected `policy`, the current `keyring` and the verification moment, reading and writing no file and modifying no argument. It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, the original item order with each report's `id` positionally bound to its item, item-id uniqueness, every bound digest and the complete shape of every report — including a full structural validation and re-tally of each verified report's complete adjudication payload against the shared policy, recomputing the policy digest and rejecting a packet whose signing moment is later than the verification moment — before checking the HMAC-SHA256 against the exact current issuer/version key. A future moment, a duplicate id, a tampered report or a non-canonical encoding raises `InvalidPruneAdjudicationBatchError`, which subclasses `ValueError`; a non-bytes packet or a wrong field type raises `TypeError`; an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`; and unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. On success it returns a fresh deep copy of the authenticated payload (`issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policyDigest`, `items`, `version`); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects. The existing chain pruning, recovery and receipt verification entry points and the README command surface are unchanged.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys

from offline_coordination import replication


def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "nodeId": "local-node",
        "connectivity": "offline",
        "revision": 0,
        "pendingChanges": 0,
    }


def _emit_line(payload: object) -> None:
    """Print one compact UTF-8 JSON line with recursively sorted keys."""
    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))


def _read_run_materials(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[object, bytes] | None:
    """Read the keyring and ticket material files for ``recovery run``."""
    try:
        with open(args.keyring, "rb") as handle:
            keyring = json.loads(handle.read().decode("utf-8"))
        with open(args.ticket, "rb") as handle:
            ticket = handle.read()
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        print(f"cannot read recovery materials: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return None
    return keyring, ticket


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="offline-coordination")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("status")
    recovery = subparsers.add_parser("recovery")
    recovery.add_argument("action", choices=["check", "run", "audit"])
    recovery.add_argument("paths", nargs="+")
    recovery.add_argument("--keyring")
    recovery.add_argument("--ticket")
    recovery.add_argument("--moment", type=int)
    recovery.add_argument("--audit")
    recovery.add_argument("--after", type=int, default=0)
    recovery.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=100)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "status":
        print(json.dumps(status(), sort_keys=True))
        return 0
    try:
        if args.action == "check":
            items = replication.inspect_recovery(args.paths)
        elif args.action == "run":
            if any(
                getattr(args, name) is None
                for name in ("keyring", "ticket", "moment", "audit")
            ):
                print(
                    "recovery run requires --keyring, --ticket, --moment "
                    "and --audit",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
                return 2
            materials = _read_run_materials(args)
            if materials is None:
                return 2
            keyring, ticket = materials
            items = replication.recover_authorized(
                args.paths, keyring, ticket, args.moment, args.audit
            )
        else:
            if len(args.paths) != 1:
                print(
                    "recovery audit takes exactly one audit path",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
                return 2
            _emit_line(
                replication.export_recovery_audit(
                    args.paths[0], after=args.after, limit=args.limit
                )
            )
            return 0
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    _emit_line(items)
    return 1 if any(item["error"] is not None for item in items) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

The batch returns, in input order, fresh dicts keyed `id`, `receipt` and `error`. The receipt is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object binding the `status`, the complete plan, the `checkpoint` digest, `beforeDigest`/`afterDigest` (equal for a duplicate), the full `delete` and `retain` digests, the prune `moment` and `version` 1, signed under the exact header key. The first completion and a same-plan re-entry (an interrupted transaction whose `.prune.txn` intent is still present) return one identical signed receipt: an installed same-plan intent is completed to the original `pruned` receipt and a prepared one is rolled back and retried.

`recover_chain_prune(path)` settles one interrupted prune transaction, touching only the files its `path + ".prune.txn"` intent names. With no intent it returns `clean` without scanning artifacts, with the current archive digest (or `None` when the path is missing). A `prepared` intent rolls the source bytes back byte-for-byte from the retained predecessor (the path is removed again when it did not exist) and deletes the candidate, reporting `rolled-back`; an `installed` intent requires the current bytes to hash to `newDigest`, removes the remaining artifacts and reports `completed`; the intent is deleted last and the directory synced so a repeat returns `clean`, and every result carries the resulting digest. A non-str path raises `TypeError`; a malformed intent (wrong key set, version, phase, target, name confinement or digest binding, or a missing necessary artifact) raises `InvalidPruneError` without touching unrelated files; an `OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing propagates unchanged with the intent and artifacts retained for a retry. `InvalidPruneError` and `StalePruneError` both subclass `ValueError`. Planning and recovery read files but planning changes nothing; the existing checkpoint continuation verification, replacement chains, module commands and README command surface are unchanged.

`verify_prune_receipt(receipt, checkpoint, keyring, moment)` verifies one signed prune receipt entirely offline — only the receipt bytes, the sealing checkpoint bytes, the current keyring and a non-negative moment are consulted, no file is read and no input is modified. The receipt must be a version-1 canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds `afterDigest`, `beforeDigest`, `checkpoint`, `delete`, `moment`, the complete embedded `plan`, `retain`, `status` (`pruned` or `duplicate`) and `version`. The embedded plan must itself be the same canonical version-1 envelope, match the supplied checkpoint digest and signing identity/key version, and the receipt must repeat the plan's delete projects and retain digests exactly — a missing, extra, reordered or replaced entry is a broken binding. The checkpoint, plan and receipt signatures are all recomputed with the single key the checkpoint currently names (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`) with no fallback. The unique plan target project is located solely from the status and before/after digests (zero or several candidates reject); the verifier then regenerates that project's version-1 prune marker itself, hashes its complete bytes, and requires the recomputed digest to match both the plan target and the receipt `afterDigest` — the receipt's derived conclusion is never trusted; a `pruned` receipt's `beforeDigest` must match the source archive and a `duplicate` receipt's both digests must match the target marker. It returns a fresh dict with the fixed key order `project`, `status`, `beforeDigest`, `afterDigest`, `checkpoint`, `planDigest`, `moment` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal, independent new objects. A wrong public argument type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int) and an illegal moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal encoding, key set, version, digest, status or binding raises `InvalidPruneReceiptError` (a `ValueError` subclass, distinct from `InvalidPruneError`); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or any signature error raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_prune_receipts(items, keyring, moment)` verifies a batch of prune receipts offline. Each item holds exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes; the non-empty list, keyring and moment are pre-validated in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/field faults `TypeError`, a bool rejected as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal moment `ValueError`). Each item is then verified in strict input order and in isolation through the exact `verify_prune_receipt` rules, reported as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated`; one item's failure never stops later items. The top-level result has exactly the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1), and each report carries in fixed order `error` (`None` when verified, otherwise a definite non-empty message), `id`, `result` (a fresh single-entry result when verified, otherwise `None`) and `status`; repeated calls return equal but independent results.
## Signed prune attestations and multi-site threshold adjudication

`sign_prune_attestation(items, batch, keyring, moment, site, version)` hands the conclusion of a prune receipt batch verification to an offline adjudicator. It takes the same non-empty `items` list as `verify_prune_receipts` (each item exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the signed `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes), the authorized non-empty `batch` id, a `keyring`, the signing `moment` and the exact signing `site` and key `version`. The batch runs through the existing `verify_prune_receipts` verification in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/public-field type faults `TypeError`, a bool never posing as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong item key set, an empty batch or site or a non-positive/non-int version `ValueError`); one receipt's own failure is never raised. The `invalid` and `unauthenticated` items are kept exactly as the batch reported them — status, definite error text, a null `result` and all — and no trusted identity, project or boundary is ever filled in for them. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`. The payload binds exactly `batch`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `site` and `version` (integer 1); each item, in the original input order with no sorting, deduplication or replacement, carries exactly `checkpoint` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that item's checkpoint bytes), `id`, `receipt` (the SHA-256 of that item's receipt bytes) and `report` (that item's complete batch verification report, bound verbatim, with a verified report's result naming the same checkpoint digest). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key the keyring binds to the exact site and version with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`adjudicate_prune_attestations(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates uniquely identified site attestations into one signed threshold decision, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `attestation` bytes. The `policy` carries exactly `batch` (the authorized batch id), `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the number of sites); `keyring` and `moment` keep their existing rules and `issuer`/`version` name the adjudicator credentials. Every attestation is re-checked by the exact signing site and key version named in its payload with no fallback: a structurally illegal packet is recorded `invalid-proof`, unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature `unauthenticated`, and a wrong batch, an unauthorized site or an unauthorized key version `unauthorized` — each rejecting only that item while the others continue. For one site, a packet counts only when the complete report and every receipt/checkpoint byte digest all agree; an exact repeat of the same content is `duplicate` and different valid content from one site is a `contradiction`. Distinct sites must agree on that same complete content: any cross-site report difference or bound-digest difference is a `conflicted` fork that a majority cannot outvote. A unique conflict-free content backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted` and carries the one common complete report; the same one unique content short of the threshold stays `insufficient` but still carries that common report; a contradiction or disagreement is `conflicted`; and an `insufficient` tally with no valid vote at all binds a null report. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `attestations` (each input attestation's SHA-256 in the original input order), `issuer`, `items` (the per-attestation rows sorted stably by site then id, each carrying `conclusion`, the attestation `digest`, the authenticated `entries` or null, `id`, `keyVersion`, `reason` and `site`), `keyVersion`, `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical compact policy — sites ascending, each site's versions an ascending array), `report` (the common complete `{items, version}` batch report, or null), `status` and `version` (integer 1); the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact adjudicator key. Parameter, container or public-field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, or an illegal batch, policy, threshold, moment, site or version raises `ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_prune_adjudication(adjudication, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such a decision entirely offline from just the decision bytes, the expected `policy`, the current `keyring` and the verification moment, reading and writing no file and modifying no argument. It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes the policy digest, and re-tallies the bound per-attestation rows purely from the signed payload: the original-order attestation digest bindings, the site/id row ordering, same-site duplicate and contradiction markings, cross-site report and digest agreement, the threshold outcome and the claimed common report — any structure, digest, ordering or tally mismatch raises `InvalidPruneAdjudicationError`, which subclasses `ValueError`. It then checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the *current* keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects the decision with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. On success it returns a fresh dict equal to the authenticated payload (`attestations`, `issuer`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `policyDigest`, `report`, `status`, `version`); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects sharing no mutable structure. A non-bytes adjudication or a field of the wrong type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int) and an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`.

`verify_prune_adjudications(items, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty batch of those decisions offline and in strict input order, in isolation. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and the `adjudication` bytes; the whole batch structure, policy, keyring and moment are validated before any adjudication is parsed, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/field type faults `TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`, with policy, keyring and moment keeping their single-entry classification). One decision's failure never stops later items or changes an earlier report. Each item is reported in input order as `verified`, `invalid` (a structure or binding fault, including a tampered status or common report) or `unauthenticated` (unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature), with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`; a failure keeps a definite, non-empty copy of the original exception text and a null result, and a verified item's result is a fresh deep copy of the authenticated adjudication payload. The top-level result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results.

`sign_prune_adjudication_batch(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` packages one such batch verification into an offline handover packet. It takes the same non-empty `items` list as `verify_prune_adjudications` and runs that exact batch verification, so batch-level faults keep the same `TypeError`/`ValueError` classification (an empty issuer or a non-positive version additionally raises `ValueError`) while one decision's failure is never raised. The `invalid` and `unauthenticated` items are kept exactly as reported — status, definite error text and a null result — and no trusted issuer, project or prune boundary is filled in from unauthenticated content. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical compact policy), `items` and `version` (integer 1). Each item, in the original input order with no sorting, deduplication or replacement, carries exactly `id`, `digest` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that item's original adjudication bytes) and `report` (that item's complete batch verification report, including the full authenticated adjudication payload when verified, bound verbatim). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact issuer/version key; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_prune_adjudication_batch(packet, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks a handover packet entirely offline from just the packet bytes, the expected `policy`, the current `keyring` and the verification moment, reading and writing no file and modifying no argument. It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, the original item order with each report's `id` positionally bound to its item, item-id uniqueness, every bound digest and the complete shape of every report — including a full structural validation and re-tally of each verified report's complete adjudication payload against the shared policy, recomputing the policy digest and rejecting a packet whose signing moment is later than the verification moment — before checking the HMAC-SHA256 against the exact current issuer/version key. A future moment, a duplicate id, a tampered report or a non-canonical encoding raises `InvalidPruneAdjudicationBatchError`, which subclasses `ValueError`; a non-bytes packet or a wrong field type raises `TypeError`; an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`; and unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. On success it returns a fresh deep copy of the authenticated payload (`issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policyDigest`, `items`, `version`); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects. The existing chain pruning, recovery and receipt verification entry points and the README command surface are unchanged.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys

from offline_coordination import replication


def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "nodeId": "local-node",
        "connectivity": "offline",
        "revision": 0,
        "pendingChanges": 0,
    }


def _emit_line(payload: object) -> None:
    """Print one compact UTF-8 JSON line with recursively sorted keys."""
    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))


def _read_run_materials(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[object, bytes] | None:
    """Read the keyring and ticket material files for ``recovery run``."""
    try:
        with open(args.keyring, "rb") as handle:
            keyring = json.loads(handle.read().decode("utf-8"))
        with open(args.ticket, "rb") as handle:
            ticket = handle.read()
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        print(f"cannot read recovery materials: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return None
    return keyring, ticket


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="offline-coordination")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("status")
    recovery = subparsers.add_parser("recovery")
    recovery.add_argument("action", choices=["check", "run", "audit"])
    recovery.add_argument("paths", nargs="+")
    recovery.add_argument("--keyring")
    recovery.add_argument("--ticket")
    recovery.add_argument("--moment", type=int)
    recovery.add_argument("--audit")
    recovery.add_argument("--after", type=int, default=0)
    recovery.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=100)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "status":
        print(json.dumps(status(), sort_keys=True))
        return 0
    try:
        if args.action == "check":
            items = replication.inspect_recovery(args.paths)
        elif args.action == "run":
            if any(
                getattr(args, name) is None
                for name in ("keyring", "ticket", "moment", "audit")
            ):
                print(
                    "recovery run requires --keyring, --ticket, --moment "
                    "and --audit",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
                return 2
            materials = _read_run_materials(args)
            if materials is None:
                return 2
            keyring, ticket = materials
            items = replication.recover_authorized(
                args.paths, keyring, ticket, args.moment, args.audit
            )
        else:
            if len(args.paths) != 1:
                print(
                    "recovery audit takes exactly one audit path",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
                return 2
            _emit_line(
                replication.export_recovery_audit(
                    args.paths[0], after=args.after, limit=args.limit
                )
            )
            return 0
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    _emit_line(items)
    return 1 if any(item["error"] is not None for item in items) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
